reason: A locator action while a JavaScript dialog is open: cua fails it at once with dialog_open and the sentence naming tab.getJsDialog(), where the vendor retries until its selector deadline ("Playwright selector deadline exceeded"). Decision Log 2026-10-13 (session, on the live dialog behaviour); acceptance 4.

evaluate runs in the page's main world (the spec's "Lifted"; acceptance 3): cua's script can set document.title, fetch and navigate, where the vendor's read-only membrane refuses ("Cannot set property title ... which has only a getter", "fetch is not a function"). A script interrupted after its one dispatch (a reload, a navigation, the budget) fails on cua with evaluate_interrupted's sentence, the fixture's counter at 1; the vendor's never reaches the counter. The no-replay rule, the spec's "What the service keeps, lifts and drops".

The clamp's maximum is 120,000 ms on cua (the spec's "Lifted"; acceptance 2): a caller's timeoutMs above 3 s raises the budget of evaluate and of locator actions, where the vendor caps every budget at 3 s and fails at its deadline.

Two fills started together in one document: cua selects and pastes each field in one operation of the virtual clipboard's queue and checks the paste against the field it prepared, so each value lands in its own field; the vendor selects both fields before either paste, so both pastes land in the field focused last (M1c whole-branch review, P1).

cua_type after focusing an input inside a cross-site (out-of-process) frame: cua pastes into the focused frame, so the text lands in the child's field and the parent page sees no paste; the vendor evaluates its paste in the top document, so the paste event reaches the parent at the frame element and the child's field stays empty. A departure in cua's favour (M1c whole-branch review P1; Decision Log 2026-10-14).

waitForLoadState with timeoutMs 0 on a loaded, network-idle page: on cua a zero budget is one observation (the M1b ruling), so a load state or network idleness that already holds succeeds; the vendor's zero timer fires before its first observation and it fails with its timeout sentence. A departure in cua's favour (M1c whole-branch review P2; Decision Log 2026-10-14).

Two tabs, each with its own download wait armed, download the same URL at once: on cua each wait gets its own download (a started download is owned by the earliest-armed matching wait, the next by the next), so the two paths differ; the vendor matches a started download by URL for every waiting tab, so one download reaches both waits and both report the same path. A departure in cua's favour (M2 task 1 review, download-start ownership; Decision Log 2026-10-14).
